name: ambiguity
description: Profile C's reference machine: a dead claim with an open attempt is ambiguous, ambiguity is never due work, and settled work stays settled.

actions.init: A fresh InMemoryMachine; claim() one row and keep its token
actions.startAttempt: InMemoryMachine.start_attempt(row, token): the attempt recorded before the provider call
actions.inspect: Read state_of, open_attempt and due_work_ids without changing anything

mutants.name: shipped-9aa6ff2
mutants.description: The exact InMemoryMachine.resolve_stalled shipped at 9aa6ff2, before the fix: settling clears the attempt, so the next sweep re-arms the settled row READY and its applied effect becomes due work again

mutants.name: blind-retry
mutants.description: The reaper re-arms every dead claim, including one whose provider call may already have applied

mutants.name: ambiguous-redispatch
mutants.description: Ambiguous rows appear in the ordinary due-work selection, so the sweep re-sends a maybe-applied effect

bugs_found.summary: Profile C's reference machine re-armed a settled row on the next reaper sweep, putting an already-applied effect back into due work; invariant 6 never ran the reaper on settled work, so adopters with the same reaper passed
bugs_found.found_by: a state-machine audit of the references, confirmed by replaying claim, attempt, expire, resolve, evidence and a second sweep against the real InMemoryMachine

limits: One claimed row. The reaper runs only on an expired lease, and late evidence arrives only for an ambiguous or settled row: whether a live claim may be resolved, and whether evidence may settle a still-claimed row, are open design questions this model does not decide.
This contracts the reference machine the profile C proofs are calibrated against, not an adopter's binding; adopters are judged by the proofs in crash_ambiguity.py.
shipped-9aa6ff2 runs resolve-9aa6ff2.py.txt, the pre-fix reaper copied verbatim from 9aa6ff2 and pinned by SHA-256 in adapter.py.
